However, the headline and rationale contradict each other, and several claims go beyond the evidence or are unsupported.","problems":["The note-check figures (problems 36%, late 2%, unsigned 0%, data 7%) and the 'no audit trail received' claim are not on the evidence card; they cannot be verified from the card, and 36 was flagged by the number check. They may come from tool output, but this cannot be confirmed here.","'Repeated-time flags' are mentioned but no corresponding number is given; this claim is unsupported.","The 'better than comparison providers' framing rests on 1 of 18 claims (6% vs 9%), which is a tiny sample; the summary does not say the difference is statistically meaningless.","The summary says the pattern is 'consistent with upcoding' and also 'would normally point toward legitimate complexity', which is muddled; the rationale conflicts with the 'conflict' headline.","Examples C0065099, C0065101 and C0066276 are described as UTI, follow-up visits and back pain, but C0066276 is R10.9 (abdominal pain), not back pain; the diagnosis description is loose. Z09 is a follow-up exam code, which is fine, but the back pain example does not map to the cited claims.","The cited_claim_ids list omits claims named in the text (C0065099, C0065101, C0066276), so the citations are inconsistent with the text.","Only 1 of 45 documented claims is below billed, and the next step to start with C0065038 is reasonable, but C0065061 has no documentation, so requesting its chart is fine but it is not an example of documented support."]}
